decision: ran it single-agent with self-review, no pi-subagents tool in this session
why: the delegation tool is not installed here

decision: seven units, small view fixes first, then API-backed features each checked on the dev server
why: cheap wins first, then each feature proves its API calls against a real server

decision: post row click opens its thread; text stays selectable and shrinks to its width so the rest of the row takes the click
why: mygo selectable text keeps the press, and asking it for Clicked turns off selection (tried in a scratch test)

decision: system posts get a drawn Mattermost-style avatar and the name System
why: the webapp heads them so; the app icon is a chat bubble, not the logo

decision: parse OpenGraph and image embeds from post metadata, attachments and override_icon_url from props; draw them as the webapp; fetch web images without the token unless same host
why: webhook and bot posts mostly use attachments, so a link preview alone would miss the user case
evidence: internal/mm/wire_test.go, /tmp/frames/previews.png, live metadata from the dev server via /tmp/p1.py

decision: added mm calls for channel, category, member and integration management and checked each against the dev server before any UI
why: the riskiest unknowns were server semantics (does moving a channel take it out of its old category, does set_unread move counts, may a member convert a channel)
result: pass; members cannot convert to private by default

decision: one dialog field holding a typed dialog (text, confirm, rename, create, browse, add members, members, integrations); one channel menu builder serves the sidebar right click, its hover button and the header
why: one source of truth for the menu items, and only one modal shows at a time

decision: used native menus (Element.Menu and ContextMenu) rather than drawn popovers
why: the post menu already uses the native context menu, and mygo Tester can drive native menus

decision: MoveToCategory now takes the channel out of every other category in one bulk PUT, as the webapp does
why: the real window showed Unfavorite did nothing: the server keeps a channel in every category that lists it, and my first API test only looked at the first match
evidence: TestParityUIChannels, /tmp/p2.py, categoryOf now demands exactly one category

decision: an empty Favorites category hides
why: the webapp hides it; the e2e frame showed a bare FAVORITES header

decision: ran scripts/realwindow.sh on a debug build, then hovered a channel, opened members and clicked a post in the real window
why: prove it on the real product, not only the headless tester; the first run failed because the display was asleep, so caffeinate -u keeps it awake
result: 18/18 twice, one run 17/18 with the emoji Tab check flaking

decision: the header channel button is labeled with the channel name and channel menu, and realwindow.sh reads the name from it
why: the name sat inside a button labeled only Channel menu, so the snapshot and screen readers lost it

decision: archived the parity channel my first failed API run left on the dev server
why: it shifted the sidebar order that the Option+Up check expects

decision: new run for 0.2.1: account menu and a click on post text opening its thread
why: user request after 0.2.0

decision: watch the text with ObserveInput: a press and release within 4 px opens the thread after the frame, a link click in that frame cancels it
why: mygo ObserveInput sees the pointer over selectable text without taking it, so selection and drags keep working

decision: drawn PopoverMenuButton with item Content for the header, status dots and icons; DND submenu with end times; custom status and profile dialogs
why: matches the webapp look and the Tester drives drawn menus

decision: the avatar picture rounds itself instead of relying on the clip
why: in the real window the clip left it square inside the drawn menu

decision: added mm calls for search, saved, pinned, reminders, edit history, threads, commands, custom emoji, GM, channel roles, restore, archived, to public, bookmarks, notify props, account security, invites and category fields, all checked against the dev server first
why: same order as round 1: server semantics before UI
result: pass; bookmarks need an Enterprise license, restore needs an admin

decision: one RHS panel slot (search, mentions, saved, pinned, channel info) under the thread, Threads as a center view on the server, settings as one tabbed dialog, themes as a table of looks
why: each new surface fits one existing slot instead of new booleans in View

decision: regenerated the emoji table with categories and skin tones from iamcal 16.0.0, Mattermost tone names (name_light_skin_tone)
why: the picker needs categories; names checked against server model/emoji_data.go

decision: the app shows images and text or code files itself, and sends PDFs and other files to Quick Look
why: mygo has no PDF view; Shell.PreviewItem is the native preview

decision: view tests, the API and UI tests of round 3 against the dev server, the full e2e suite and realwindow.sh pass
why: prove each feature on the server and in the real window before the release

decision: right click on the text of a post shows Copy and the post actions together
why: the text now fills the row, and its own Copy menu hid the post menu (found by the e2e test)

decision: the thread header drops Copy link and uses a small Follow button
why: the close button left the RHS in a 1200 wide window
